quest.title: The Millennial Mountains
quest.description: According to a local legend at The Chasm, one may be able to obtain the "treasure of the Millelith" by offering six items before a memorial.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: O great Millelith heroes, please see to it that The Chasm does not act up these few days!

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: And may we be safe and sound as we descend into the mines this time, and may those comrades of ours who no longer come to mine also fare well in their respective paths. Protect us, brave Millelith, protect us...

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Hmm? What is it? Can I help you?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Well, I'm praying at this Millelith memorial. I mean, it looks like a pile of unassuming rocks, but it's actually been here for five hundred years now!

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: The Chasm is under the protection of the Millelith, so every time we have people descend into the mines, we will pray here for the heroic souls of those who have passed to protect us.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: They have long since turned into elements and become one with the mine, so when we pray for their protection, we're also showing our reverence to The Chasm itself, you know?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: The ancients said that "the earth has a spirit, and the elements have souls." Those who sacrificed their lives so that we might live watch over us in similar fashion. So I believe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Five hundred years ago?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: That's right. Back then, a dark calamity swallowed The Chasm, and Rex Lapis commanded the Millelith to stand guard over the ore veins.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: That was a terrible battle. Led by a Yaksha, the Millelith came forth to stem the tide.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: In the end, a group of them led the foe into the depths of The Chasm, and thus quelled the unrest.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: It is said that this memorial was set up for them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Paimon didn't think that these ugly stones would have such history...

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Hehe, don't disrespect the fallen, little one.

choices.text: Don't you worry, this little one won't bite.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who's a "little one"!?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Hehe, whatever the case, this is a pretty familiar story to anyone who grew up around The Chasm as we did... There are many versions of the tale, too, which sprung up over time.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: If you were to talk to someone else, they might tell you a different story. Maybe this is the charm of history? Not that I'm particularly cultured, mind, but I'm just saying, y'know?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Ah, yeah, speaking of which, there's always been a rumor going about. It says that these stones hide another secret that might lead a discerning person to treasure that the Millelith left behind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Treasure that they left behind?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could you give us some details? Let's just say that... Paimon's interest has been piqued!

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Eh, it's just a rumor, but it's one that's got to do with the Millelith member who created this memorial in the first place.

choices.text: Didn't the miners set this memorial up?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Nah. The one that the miners set up is elsewhere, and it isn't anywhere as large as this one.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: The battle ended, but many of their comrades now rest eternally in the depths of The Chasm, together with that nameless Yaksha...

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: One of the soldiers fell from a great height while helping to evacuate the miners and beat back the enemy, injuring his spine and becoming unable to move on his own power as a result...

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: But later, it is said that he was not daunted by his circumstances, instead becoming a self-taught and much-famed doctor who would help those in the same situation as himself.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: It is said that this memorial was something he set up to remember his comrades by after he had obtained a Vision.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: His story would gradually fade from history, being replaced with tales of the "Millelith's treasure" and the "Yaksha's inheritance."

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Those are just baseless tales. We miners generally prefer to keep our feet firmly planted, so I don't give much credence to these tales. Still...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: No, it's nothing, I just mean that I won't laugh if you do actually go looking for that treasure.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: I've given it some thought, and it occurred to me that while the tales of treasure might all be false, they exist as a way for generations of people to ensure that stories are passed down and not forgotten by later generations.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Whatever the case, the one who offers up six items lost within The Chasm before this stone will be awarded the gifts of the Millelith — that's how the story goes.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: And these six items are...

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: The Helm of Warding, which may defend one from rockfalls...

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: The Cup of Commons, made to memorialize comradeship...

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: The Skyfeather, the symbol of lofty ideals...

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: The Warrior's Spear, used to fend off the foe...

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: The "Flower of Farsight," which grew upon the cliffs of The Chasm...

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: And... the "Sundial of Ages," used to remember the bygone past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that wasn't confusing at all, no sir!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You sure this wasn't all made up by people later?

choices.text: So these items can all be found within The Chasm?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: I've got no clue. Maybe they were all made up — that would certainly explain why no one's found the legendary treasure this whole time!

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Ah, yes, speaking of which... There was another memorial that I mentioned, yes? *sigh* Everyone's just busied themselves with their own separate things after The Chasm was closed. No one's kept that place clean, I'll bet.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Could you help me go over there and just tidy the place up? Just a little will do...

choices.text: So this was the work of a Millelith soldier?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Indeed, both the Millelith and the miners at The Chasm set memorials up back then.

choices.text: Indeed, disrespecting the fallen is bad manners.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, sorry...

talks.objective: Look for offerings to place before the memorial

dialogues.speaker: Stone Tablet
dialogues.text: (This small stone tablet has the following words inscribed on it...)

dialogues.speaker: Stone Tablet
dialogues.text: ..."During the battle at The Chasm, I lost the use of my four limbs and thus was forced to dictate these words for someone else to record and carve here."...

dialogues.speaker: Stone Tablet
dialogues.text: ..."I survived that fierce battle, but each night where I thought of our fallen comrades was a sleepless one. And with my body in this state, oh, how I detested the fact that I was not privileged to join them."...

dialogues.speaker: Stone Tablet
dialogues.text: ..."I attempted to join them, only to have Rex Lapis hear of it and reprimand me, waking me from my stupor."...

dialogues.speaker: Stone Tablet
dialogues.text: ..."Alas, for I can no longer make use of his gift of Millelith armor and equipment. They shall only accumulate dust if left in my keeping, and so I leave them here for someone fated to come and claim them."...

dialogues.speaker: Stone Tablet
dialogues.text: ..."Everyone, though we can no longer do so in this life, let us be comrades again in the next. Let us then share the wine of sworn brotherhood once more, and defend Liyue from its foes!"...

talks.objective: Look for offerings to place before the memorial

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Oh, wow, you really found it! So... this is the "treasure of the Millelith," then?

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Now, I've got no clue what's in there, but I'm sure that the soldier who left that treasure behind would be pleased to know that it was found.

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: It's been five hundred years since that disaster... When I think about how this place was once the site of such an intense battle, one in which countless forebears of ours sacrificed themselves, I can't help but wonder...

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Did any of those people who went into battle alongside the Lord of Geo think that they would be remembered by people across the centuries?

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Did they ever doubt or falter in their duties? And as for those who never gained a Vision, how did they remain loyal to a god who never showed them favor, even until death?

choices.text: Their god never left their side.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Yes, you're right. Those with Visions, those without... We are all working towards a future with limitless potential. I mean, that's what they call motivation, am I right?

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: We're the same. We're not here for the good times in the past, or for some self-realization in the present... But we do this to support one another in leaving something of ourselves behind in the times we live in.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Maybe someday in the far future, The Chasm will also become our memorial.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: The pits and the valleys, the sweat of generations of miners... They all bear witness to the tough road we have chosen.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Just like this memorial, this place will be here a hundred, even a thousand years from now, as testament to the fact that the sacrifices made here were not in vain.

response.speaker: Wang
response.text: Hehe, well, I'm not going to live to see that happen, obviously, but if someone does come here someday to toast us poor miners long after we're gone, that would be more than enough.

choices.text: They were loyal to their own decisions as well.

talks.objective: Look for offerings to place before the memorial

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: The items you need to find are the Helm, the Feather, the Cup, the Sundial, the Flower, and the Spear.

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: That said, no one's found them all to this day, so...

talks.objective: Look for offerings to place before the memorial

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: It is said that the Flower of Farsight will only make itself known to those with such lofty desires that they might seem crazy to some, and thus is not something ordinary people can witness. Hmm, I wonder what sort of flower that would be?

talks.objective: Look for offerings to place before the memorial

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: I've heard that the Skyfeather can only be obtained from an eagle on a certain mountaintop. That said, never in all my years have I seen someone who can pluck a feather from an eagle...

talks.objective: Look for offerings to place before the memorial

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: They say that the Sundial of Ages would be remembered by all, such that time's passage would not cause it to lose its luster. Perhaps it has never been forgotten or lost after all?

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: The items you need to find are the Helm, the Feather, the Cup, the Sundial, the Flower, and the Spear.

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: That said, no one's found them all to this day, so...

talks.objective: Offer the items before the memorial

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: I've heard it said that the Cup of Commons will regain its dignity someday, even if it is obtained by bandits and crooks, or becomes a lowly guest at a humble table... But what does that even mean?

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: The Helm of Warding is said to rest in the room of an ordinary person, yet may not be summoned forth by anyone but a hero... Well, this was a story I used to fall asleep to, so...

talks.objective: Talk to Wang about the treasure

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Tell me about the "Flower of Farsight."

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Tell me about the Skyfeather.

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Tell me about the Sundial of Ages.

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Tell me about the Cup of Commons.

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Tell me about the Helm of Warding.

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Tell me about the Warrior's Spear.

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: The Warrior's Spear is rumored to have been set up on a lone cliff, awaiting a valiant soul equal to it. Only then will it be content to once again enter time's eternal flow... Hah, what an exaggerated legend...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you...

dialogues.speaker: Wang
dialogues.text: Yes, see you... But take care now. The Chasm is still quite a dangerous place.
